title: Trace an order through retry, replay protection, and compensation
description: Switch scenarios to see which path executes after a transient failure, duplicate start, terminal payment error, or failed compensation. The idempotency ledger represents application state outside Step Functions.

nodes.label: Order API
nodes.detail: Starts the workflow with a caller-provided business identifier and returns an operation reference instead of claiming the order is already complete.

nodes.label: Standard workflow
nodes.detail: Persists workflow state, applies explicit retry and catch rules, and records the execution path. It does not own the payment or inventory records.

nodes.label: Idempotency ledger
nodes.detail: Claims a stable order ID and stores operation status so a duplicate start can return the existing outcome without repeating business effects.

nodes.label: Inventory service
nodes.detail: Reserves stock with the order ID as an idempotency key and can release that reservation during compensation.

nodes.label: Bounded retrier
nodes.detail: Retries named transient failures with a timeout, maximum attempts, capped backoff, and jitter before the Catch path runs.

nodes.label: Payment service
nodes.detail: Uses the order ID as the payment operation key so an ambiguous response or explicit Task retry cannot create a second charge.

nodes.label: Order record
nodes.detail: Stores completed, duplicate, compensated, or failed status independently from workflow logs so callers can query durable business state.

nodes.label: Release inventory
nodes.detail: Reverses the successful reservation after payment cannot complete. It is an idempotent business action, not a database rollback.

nodes.label: Operations queue
nodes.detail: Receives a terminal incident with the order, execution, original error, and compensation result when automation cannot restore a known business state.

scenarios.label: Normal order
scenarios.summary: The workflow claims the order, reserves inventory, charges with a stable operation key, and publishes a completed business record.
scenarios.result: The caller can query a durable completed order. The workflow history explains the orchestration path; the order, inventory, and payment systems remain authoritative for their own state.

scenarios.label: Bounded retry
scenarios.summary: The first payment attempt returns a named transient service error. The retrier waits with capped backoff and jitter, then repeats the same logical charge key.
scenarios.result: A later attempt succeeds without a second business charge because the payment service recognizes the stable idempotency key. After the maximum attempt count, Catch would move to compensation instead.

scenarios.label: Duplicate start
scenarios.summary: A caller or event starts the same logical order again. The conditional ledger claim finds the existing order before inventory or payment runs.
scenarios.result: The duplicate follows the existing-result path and creates no new reservation or charge. A workflow execution guarantee alone would not provide this cross-execution business deduplication.

scenarios.label: Compensation
scenarios.summary: Inventory succeeds, but payment reaches a terminal business error after the bounded retry policy. Catch invokes the release operation.
scenarios.result: The reservation is released and the order is marked compensated. This restores an understood business state; it does not erase the original payment failure or workflow history.

scenarios.label: Terminal failure
scenarios.summary: Payment fails and the inventory release also exhausts its bounded retry policy. The workflow cannot truthfully claim success or full compensation.
scenarios.result: The execution ends in a terminal failure and sends complete recovery context to operators. The order stays in an explicit manual-recovery state until inventory and payment records are reconciled.
